name: VAR
description: VAR estimates the variance based on a sample of a population, using the n-1 denominator (Bessel's correction). It is the legacy compatibility version of VAR.S.
tldr: Sample variance (n-1) of a set of numbers.

parameters.name: number1
parameters.description: The first number, range, or reference in the sample.

parameters.name: number2
parameters.description: Additional numbers, ranges, or references (optional, up to 255 total arguments).

basicExample.explanation: The mean is 30; the sum of squared deviations is 1000, divided by 5-1 gives a sample variance of 250.

advancedExamples.title: Sample from a range
advancedExamples.description: Compute the variance of scores in A2:A11
advancedExamples.explanation: Uses the 10 sampled values with n-1 (9) in the denominator.

advancedExamples.title: Sample vs population
advancedExamples.explanation: VAR divides by 4 (n-1) while VARP divides by 5 (n), so the population version is smaller. VAR is the square of STDEV for the same data.

howItWorks: VAR computes the sample variance as the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by (n-1). The n-1 divisor (Bessel's correction) yields an unbiased estimate of the population variance from a sample. Text and logical values in references are ignored, and VAR equals STDEV squared.

howToSteps.name: Select sample
howToSteps.text: Gather the numeric sample values in cells or as arguments.

limitations: Assumes the data is a sample, not the entire population; use VARP for a whole population.
Ignores text and logical values inside ranged references, reducing the effective count.
Requires at least two numeric values, otherwise returns #DIV/0!.

commonErrors.cause: Fewer than two numeric values were supplied.
commonErrors.fix: Provide at least two data points.

commonErrors.cause: The data is the full population but n-1 was used.
commonErrors.fix: Use VARP (or VAR.P) for an entire population.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: VAR behaves the same in Google Sheets as a sample variance.

faq.question: What is the difference between VAR and VARP?
faq.answer: VAR divides by n-1 (sample), VARP divides by n (population).

faq.question: Is VAR the same as VAR.S?
faq.answer: Functionally yes; VAR.S is the modern replacement for the legacy VAR function.

faq.question: How is VAR related to STDEV?
faq.answer: VAR is the square of STDEV for the same data set.
